events.title: Otto von Bismarck Is Born
events.description: Otto von Bismarck was born into a Prussian landowning family at Schönhausen. He grew up to become the statesman who steered Prussia through a series of wars and brought the German states together under one empire.
events.significance: Bismarck's diplomacy and 'realpolitik' created the unified German Empire in 1871 and shaped the balance of power in Europe for decades.

events.title: U.S. Forces Land on Okinawa
events.description: On Easter Sunday, American troops began the largest amphibious assault of the Pacific War on the island of Okinawa. They met surprisingly little resistance at first, but the campaign that followed became long and costly.
events.significance: Okinawa was the last major battle of World War II in the Pacific. It put Allied forces within striking distance of the Japanese home islands.

events.title: Apple Computer Is Founded
events.description: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne founded Apple Computer Co. in California. The company began by selling the Apple I, a hand-built personal computer.
events.significance: Apple grew into one of the world's most influential companies. Its computers, phones and software changed how people work, communicate and create.

events.title: Marvin Gaye Is Killed
events.description: Soul singer Marvin Gaye was shot and killed at his family home in Los Angeles by his father, the day before his 45th birthday. His death shocked the music world.
events.significance: Gaye's music, including 'What's Going On' and 'Let's Get It On', remains a landmark of soul and R&B, and his loss is still mourned as a great cultural tragedy.

events.title: Nunavut Becomes a Canadian Territory
events.description: Canada created Nunavut by dividing the Northwest Territories, giving the Inuit people a territory of their own in the Arctic.
events.significance: Nunavut was a landmark in Indigenous self-government in Canada. It was the first major change to the country's map since Newfoundland joined in 1949.
